published_statement: 1508.07161 abstract p.1 (verbatim, DOCKET 65 capture): 'While the cross-over is smooth, it is very well defined with a width of only ~ 5 GeV. We measure the cross-over temperature from the maximum of the susceptibility of the Higgs condensate, with the result T_c = 159.5 +/- 1.5 GeV.' Sec. VII p.8: 'we obtain T_c = 159.6 +/- 0.1 +/- 1.5 GeV, where the first error is due to the statistical accuracy of the lattice computation and the second one is the estimated uncertainty of the effective theory approach'. fn.1 p.1: 'Although there is no real symmetry breaking phase transition, we use the conventional labels "broken" and "symmetric"'. p.1: first order only for m_H <~ 72 GeV. 1404.3565 p.1: 'a smooth cross-over from the symmetric phase at T > T_c, where the (expectation value of the) Higgs field was approximately zero, to the broken phase at T < T_c GeV where it is finite'; p.3: 'If the temperature is below T_c, v^2(T) is approximately linear in T, and at T > T_c, it is close to zero' and 'because of additive renormalization, v^2(T) can become negative'; abstract: 'the cross-over is sharply defined at T_c = (159 +/- 1) GeV'. 1206.2942 p.4: 'Note that (in unitary gauge) the masses of the W+/- and Z0 weak vector bosons and the fermions are proportional to phi.'

rederivation.outcome: All 13 checks pass (exit 0). A: 160 GeV = 1.8567e15 K and 159.5 GeV = 1.8509e15 K reproduce warpfolder.py:392 and massform.py:545; 160 is inside both 159.5+/-1.5 and 159.6+/-0.1+/-1.5. B (sympy + z3, RECONSTRUCTED textbook high-T expansion, used for DIRECTION only): summing T^2/24 n_b m_b^2 + T^2/48 n_f m_f^2 over W(6) Z(3) h(1) G(3) t(12) gives m^2(T) = -mu^2 + c T^2 with c = (3g^2 + g'^2 + 4y_t^2 + 8 lam)/16; z3 proves c > 0 for every real g, g', y_t and lam > 0 (unsat of the negation; vacuity guard sat): the SM curvature at phi = 0 turns positive at high T -- heating is the symmetric direction. At the PDG-2026 capture c = 0.3978 and the mean-field T0 = 140.3 GeV, ~19 GeV below the lattice T_c: the one-loop mean-field model is too crude to reproduce the number, which is why the lattice value, not this, is the datum; the model checks direction and order only. C: m_H = 125.13 GeV exceeds the 72 GeV endpoint by 53.1 GeV. D: mass moves shift T0 by +0.12 (m_H) and +0.20 GeV (m_t). E: a bounded-below two-scalar potential (lam1 = 0.1, lam2 = 4, lam12 = -0.5) has thermal phi1^2 coefficient -0.0083 T^2 < 0: high-T restoration is a property of the SM's scalar sector, not universal. Not checkable here: the lattice T_c itself and the shape of v^2(T) near T_c (need the paper's data, not re-read).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. The DECISIVE datum for this result is the Higgs mass. Before 2012 (and before the LEP bound) the SM's thermal transition was conditional: first order for m_H <~ 72 GeV, a crossover above (1508.07161 p.1, as captured). The 1996 endpoint work lacked m_H; the datum, when it came (PDG-2026 capture: 125.13 GeV), moved the conclusion from conditional to settled crossover -- in the direction the tree uses, with a 53 GeV margin, so no plausible revision reverses it. The 2014-16 lattice authors had the discovery; their inputs were not re-read here, but the tree's current m_H and m_t shift the mean-field model's T0 by 0.12 and 0.20 GeV, an order below their own 1.5 GeV effective-theory systematic. What remains lacking is BSM data: the result is for ONE Higgs doublet; an extended scalar sector with negative cross couplings could fail to restore (check E) or turn the crossover first order. No datum excludes such a sector and none requires it; that is a NAMED hypothesis (SM only), not a moved datum. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the missing datum arrived and confirmed. Evidence for a flaw: none in the physics; the discrepancies found are the tree's wording ('<phi> -> 0' at T_c; 'restores'; 'un-generates the fermion masses'), each stronger than the source.
grade_evidence: The direction the tree needs STANDS: in the SM the high-T side is the symmetric-labelled side (z3-proved positivity of the thermal curvature coefficient; lattice crossover at 159.5 +/- 1.5 GeV, 1508.07161 as captured), and the tree's 160 GeV is 0.33 sigma from it; no moved datum moves it (m_H 125.13 vs the 72 GeV endpoint). But the tree states it on a larger class than the source: (i) '<phi> -> 0' where the source says 'approximately zero' (renormalized v^2 can be negative); (ii) AT T_EW ~ 160 GeV = T_c, where the source's T_c is the susceptibility maximum in the middle of a ~5 GeV crossover -- approximately zero is for T > T_c; (iii) 'restores the symmetry' where the source says there is no real symmetry-breaking transition (fn.1); (iv) 'un-generates the fermion masses' where the source basis is tree-level vev-generated masses only (thermal masses not addressed); (v) the SM-only hypothesis is unnamed, and restoration is model-dependent (check E). Holding the result on the narrower class -- SM, equilibrium, T a few GeV above ~160 GeV, vev-generated masses approximately zero -- still gives FLASH_IS_A_RECONSTRUCTION_MECHANISM = False on reason (a), because the objection is about direction, which survives every narrowing. Not WRONG: nothing here is refuted; the discrepancies are wording, recorded not repaired. Caveat on the read: the source was not re-read in this stage (quota/egress); the grade rests on DOCKET 65's verbatim captures.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners restate (a) as 'in the SM, for T above the ~160 GeV crossover (width ~5 GeV), the Higgs condensate is approximately zero and the vev-generated masses approximately vanish; there is no true transition' -- or a re-read of 1508.07161 showing v^2 already approximately zero AT the susceptibility maximum (not expected from 1404.3565 p.3's 'approximately linear below T_c'). To DATA-DEPENDENT: evidence of an extended scalar sector (e.g. a second doublet or singlet with negative cross couplings) that alters or prevents high-T restoration. To OPEN: if the DOCKET 65 captures were found not to be verbatim on re-reading 1508.07161/1404.3565 at source. Nothing found here would move it to WRONG.
